# ReqPilot — P3 Extraction & Classification

**Roadmap phase:** P3 (`docs/01-analysis.md` §P) · **Modules:** M4 LLM gateway, M3 (agent roles #3 and #5, the
P3 subset of `analysis_graph`), M6/M9 (repository integration, review queue), M11 (masking seam), M12 (E1 harness)

**Status: P3 COMPLETE — ROADMAP EXIT PASSED**

*Updated 2026-09-22 (§20).* E1 was computed with the real model (OpenAI `gpt-5.6-luna`) against
**E1-SYNTHETIC-v1**. That is a **synthetic reference benchmark**, generated by an AI assistant and reviewed by the sole
project author. It is **not** an independently annotated gold standard, and the result is not evidence of real-world
accuracy.

| Level | Status |
|---|---|
| **P3 implementation** | **Complete**, including the OpenAI provider (§19). Verified offline, against a live PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector, and with opt-in real-model checks (§17, §19) |
| **P3 roadmap exit** (analysis §P) | **Passed**, with two documented, author-approved deviations (§20.6) |

The exit criteria, and how each was met:

- **"E1 computed against gold transcript #1."** Met: precision, recall and F1 are all **0.967** (58/60), computed by
  the unchanged harness (§20). The "gold transcript #1" slot is filled by a synthetic reference benchmark, not an
  independently annotated gold set. This is deviation 1.
- **"This run re-baselines ET-07."** Met: ET-07 is re-baselined and **kept at F1 ≥ 0.75** (§20.4).
- **"...and sets targets for E2–E9."** Met by interpretation: each E2–E9 target is set from that metric's own first
  measurement in P5–P9, as O.1 prescribes ("set from measured behaviour after P3–P7, not guessed"). This is
  deviation 2.
- **"Offline fixture tests pass."** Met (§17).

> **The LLM proposes; deterministic code disposes.** P3 is the first phase in which a model's output enters
> ReqPilot. It enters only as a typed proposal:
>
> - the gateway checks it against a schema;
> - deterministic validation checks its sources, form and labels;
> - the P1 repository stores what survives, through the P1 lifecycle;
> - a human reviews anything the rules flag.
>
> The model cannot set an identifier, a lifecycle state, an approval, a risk level or a regulatory mapping. The
> contract has nowhere to put them, and nothing downstream would accept them.

---

## 1. P3 scope

The approved P3 deliverable (analysis §P) is: *"LLM gateway, extraction, classification, confidence signals,
review queue"*. It is the first AI capability, in **batch mode**. It covers:

- **The M4 LLM gateway**, the single model boundary. It provides:
  - the prompt registry;
  - trust-class assembly;
  - egress guards;
  - structured output with one bounded repair;
  - retries;
  - token and cost accounting;
  - model and prompt stamping;
  - record/replay.
- **Two agent roles:** #3 Requirement Extraction and #5 Classification. Both are propose-only.
- **The F.2 validation pipeline** for their output.
- **Batch execution** as the P3 subset of `analysis_graph`, nodes 1–5 and 25 of C.3.
- **The project corpus**: source documents, and their segments with exact offsets.
- **Persistence through P1**: deterministic identifiers and guarded transitions. Nothing goes beyond `CLASSIFIED`.
- **Classification** with revisions and human overrides (`FR-CLS-003`).
- **The review-queue foundation** for AI proposals. It is **not** approval.
- **Near-duplicate handling** that keeps every source link.
- **The E1 harness**: the frozen gold set, adjudicated matching and an honest report.

**Out of scope, and absent:**

- adaptive interviews, the elicitation graph and utterances (P4);
- clarification (P4);
- quality analysis and conflict detection (P5);
- compliance, security and privacy analysis (P6);
- risk (P7);
- SDLC work (P9, P10);
- documents (P8);
- the rest of `analysis_graph`;
- production authentication;
- masking and injection detection (P11);
- few-shot learning from overrides (`FR-CLS-004`, secondary);
- any regulatory content;
- any change to P2 or ET-06.

## 4. LLM gateway architecture

`reqpilot.llm.LLMGateway` is the only way to a model. It is enforced three ways:

- an import-linter contract;
- an AST test that no module outside `llm/` constructs or imports a provider;
- a test that starting the application and building the default gateway imports no provider SDK, and that only
  `llm/openai_provider.py` imports the OpenAI SDK (§19).

```
agent role ──► LLMGateway.generate(role, prompt_name, params, content blocks, schema)
                 1. prompt registry: versioned template for this role; params validated by pattern
                 2. trust-class assembly: template + JSON-schema contract = instructions;
                    every content block fenced as data with a content-derived nonce
                 3. egress guards: no configured secret in any text; no unmasked, non-synthetic
                    project content to a provider that leaves the machine
                 4. provider call, transient failures retried with backoff (bounded)
                 5. parse JSON → Pydantic schema; on failure ONE repair (C.8): same prompt +
                    error locations; the bad output only as fenced MODEL_OUTPUT
                 6. ModelMeta: provider, model, is_model, prompt name/version/sha256, contract
                    version, tokens, latency, attempts, repaired, cost estimate → usage ledger
               ◄── StructuredResult(value | error_code + system-written message)
```

**Providers.** One network provider; the others stay offline.

- **`OpenAIProvider`** (`llm/openai_provider.py`) is the network provider, selected at P3 closure (§19). It is used
  only when `LLM_PROVIDER=openai`.
- **`StubLLMGateway`** is the P0 stub. It returns a marked placeholder that no contract accepts, so a stub run can
  only fail visibly.
- **`ScriptedProvider`** is a deterministic test double. It answers from a function, is marked `is_model = False`,
  and its output never counts towards a metric.
- **`RecordingLLMGateway`** does record and replay at the gateway boundary (ADR-012). Strict replay never calls a
  provider, and reports a missing fixture as an error.

Selecting `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` or `ollama` fails fast and names the selected provider. A provider is one class
that implements `complete`; the OpenAI provider is exactly that.

**Configuration** is explicit in `config.py` and `.env.example`:

| Setting | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | `stub` (default, offline) or `openai` |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | The provider key. It lives in the untracked `.env` only, and is required for `openai` |
| `LLM_MODEL_DEFAULT` | The model. Required for `openai`; never fixed in code |
| `LLM_BASE_URL` | Optional endpoint. Empty means the SDK's default |
| `LLM_TEMPERATURE` | Optional. Empty means the provider's default, and it is not sent |
| `LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-request timeout for the network provider |
| `LLM_MAX_RETRIES` | Bound on transient-failure retries |
| `LLM_FIXTURE_MODE` / `LLM_FIXTURE_DIR` | Record/replay mode and fixture store |
| `LLM_PRICE_INPUT_PER_1K` / `LLM_PRICE_OUTPUT_PER_1K` | Token prices. Empty means *unknown*, never zero |

**Prompts** are data files in `llm/prompts/*.yaml`: `requirement_extraction@1.0.0` and
`requirement_classification@1.0.0`.

- `registry.yaml` pins the active versions and locks each file's sha256.
- Editing a template without a new version fails at startup.
- The exact text a run used is stored once in `prompt_template` and referenced by every agent run (G.7).
- The model identity is stored in `model_version`, together with `is_model`.

**Retries and failure.**

- Transient errors are retried up to `LLM_MAX_RETRIES` times, with backoff of 0.5 s, 1 s, … up to 8 s.
- Other provider exceptions become a recorded `provider_unavailable` failure, never a crash.
- Malformed output gets exactly one repair attempt, then a `malformed_output` failure.

## 5. Extraction contract

The model's whole vocabulary is `ExtractionOutput` (`agents/contracts/extraction.py`), with `extra="forbid"`:

```
ExtractedRequirement: candidate_key (temporary label), statement, requirement_type (functional|non_functional),
  evidence[{segment_id, quote}], justification?{text, segment_id, quote}, priority?{value, segment_id, quote},
  assumptions[{text, segment_id, quote}], depends_on[key], duplicate_of[key],
  acceptance_criteria[{given, when, then}], review_signal ∈ [0,1]
```

**Deliberately absent** (`[DESIGN] D4`, F.4):

- identifier;
- lifecycle state;
- approval status;
- risk level;
- applicable regulations;
- category;
- character offsets.

An output that tries to set any of them fails the schema, visibly. After the one repair attempt, the run fails.

**Deterministic validation** (`agents/validation/extraction.py`, F.2) turns a proposal into a `ValidatedCandidate`
or a `RejectedCandidate`. Both are defined in the domain.

| Check | On failure |
|---|---|
| ≥ 1 evidence item whose quote (≥ 3 words) is found **by code** in the segment it names | Rejected (`unresolved_source`), sent to review, **never persisted as a requirement** |
| Some evidence resolves and some does not | Accepted with the resolved spans; the dropped ones are flagged for review |
| Statement begins exactly "The system shall " and is within length | Rejected (`extraction_invalid`), sent to review |
| Justification, priority and each assumption carry their own resolving quote | The field is **dropped**, recorded as a finding. Never guessed |
| `depends_on` and `duplicate_of` name other proposals in the batch | The reference is dropped and recorded |
| At most 5 criteria, each with a non-empty, bounded Given, When and Then | **All** criteria are dropped, and the version is flagged for review. Never repaired |
| The model's review signal is at or above the extraction threshold | Kept, and sent to review |
| The candidate key is not reused within the output | The repeat is rejected |

**Near-duplicates** (`FR-EXT-005`) are handled over the whole run.

- **Exact duplicates are merged by code.** An exact duplicate has the same kind and the same statement after
  normalising case, punctuation, whitespace and the shared opening. Every span of both is kept, and the merge is
  recorded on the merged candidate.
- **Near-duplicates are never merged by code.** Pairs with token-set Jaccard similarity ≥ 0.8 (provisional, in the
  ruleset) are raised as `possible_duplicate` review items instead.
  - "shall encrypt" and "shall not encrypt" score above that threshold, which is exactly why this is a question for
    a human.
- **Model-proposed duplicates** are review items too.
- **New requirements that duplicate existing ones** in the project are raised the same way (basis `existing`).
- **Merging is a human decision.** A human can merge through the review queue or the API, and a merge:
  - creates a P1 successor version of the survivor with **all** source references;
  - copies its acceptance criteria forward;
  - withdraws the duplicate through P1.

  Every source link and the original wording survive.

**The §8 schema (`FR-EXT-002`).** `GET /requirements/{id}/record` assembles all thirteen fields from where each
lives:

| §8 field | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| ID | Allocated by code |
| Statement | The current version |
| Category | The current classification revision |
| Source stakeholder | The speakers of the source spans, as written in the transcript |
| Justification, priority, assumptions | Only if the source states them |
| Dependencies | The current version |
| Acceptance criteria | The criterion rows bound to the version |
| Applicable regulations | `deferred: … (roadmap P6)` |
| Risk level | `deferred: … (roadmap P7)` |
| Confidence | The extraction review signal, with its caveat |
| Approval status | The lifecycle state |

## 6. Classification contract

`ClassificationOutput`: `labels[{category: str, review_signal ∈ [0,1], rationale}]`.

The category is a string on purpose. Each label is validated on its own, so one unknown label cannot sink the
valid ones.

- **Normalisation.** A label is accepted if it is:
  - one of the 13 values or the problem statement's spellings (`availability/reliability`, `data-management`,
    `audit/reporting`, `operational/maintenance`);
  - either half of a slash category;
  - any of those in any case or separator.

  Nothing else is accepted.
- **Rejection.** `compliance`, `legal`, `non-functional` and the like are rejected and raised as `unknown_label`.
  They are never mapped by guesswork.
- **Repeats.** A repeated category is kept once, at its first occurrence.
- **No valid label.** The classification has failed: the version stays `EXTRACTED` and gets a
  `classification_failed` review item.
- **The prompt forbids inferring `regulatory`.** It may be used only when the requirement text itself refers to a
  law or regulator, because the mapping to regulations is P6's, with evidence.

## 7. Source-span and provenance model

- **Project corpus** (G.3, J.1):
  - `source_document` holds the normalised text, content hash, type, declared sensitivity, masking status and
    masker. It is append-only.
  - `source_chunk` holds the segments.
  - Transcripts and meeting notes are split into **speaker turns** (J.3: never split a turn). Other documents are
    split into sections and paragraphs, using the J.3 sizes from `retrieval.yaml`.
  - Every segment satisfies `text == document.text[char_start:char_end]`. Its id is derived from the segment itself.
  - **No embedding is stored.** J.2 forbids unmasked text in the vector store.
- **The model never supplies offsets.** It names a segment (`S3`) and quotes it. `domain/source_spans.py` finds the
  quote in the stored segment and computes document offsets. Matching tolerates whitespace, typographic punctuation
  and then case, in that order. The recorded quote is always the **source's slice**, never the model's rendering of
  it.
- **Each source reference** on a version is `{kind: source_chunk, ref, span: [start, end], document, quote,
  speaker}`, the P1 shape extended. It is part of the governed content hash.
- **`FR-EXT-007` in three layers:**
  - a `ValidatedCandidate` cannot be constructed without spans;
  - validation rejects any proposal with none;
  - the P1 `CANDIDATE → EXTRACTED` guard requires a source reference.
- **Original wording** is the distinct resolved quotes, in document order, joined by "…".

## 8. Confidence and review policy

The review signal is **the model's own heuristic review-prioritisation signal, not a calibrated probability**
(approved Phase 0 H.1; O.2 S8). It is shown with that caveat everywhere: API, UI and the record. It is never
transformed.

The thresholds are in `rules/data/extraction.yaml` v1.0.0, all **provisional**, to be re-set from measured
behaviour after E1:

| Threshold | Value |
|---|---|
| Extraction signal | 0.5 |
| Classification signal | 0.6 |
| Near-duplicate similarity | 0.8 |

**What raises a review item:**

| Reason | Raised when | Subject |
|---|---|---|
| `malformed_output` | The model's output stayed schema-invalid after the repair | The agent run |
| `unresolved_source` | A proposal had no resolving source (rejected), or some of its evidence was dropped | The candidate, or the version |
| `extraction_invalid` | Not declarative, too long, or a reused key | The candidate |
| `low_extraction_signal` | The extraction signal is below its threshold | The version |
| `acceptance_criteria_invalid` | The proposed criteria were dropped | The version |
| `low_classification_signal` | A label's signal is below its threshold. The label is kept, marked `needs_review` | The version and the label |
| `unknown_label` | A label is outside the taxonomy | The version |
| `classification_failed` | No valid label, or the call failed | The version |
| `possible_duplicate` | Similar within the run, proposed by the model, or similar to an existing requirement | Both versions |

**Resolving.**

- Resolution is human-only (policy rule 6) and audited.
- Each reason admits only certain resolutions: `accepted`, `rejected` (a P1 withdrawal), `overridden`, `merged`,
  `kept_distinct` or `acknowledged`.
- Rejecting, overriding and merging need a note.

**The queue is not approval.** Every API item carries that notice, and the page opens with it. Resolving every
item creates no approval task and moves nothing past `CLASSIFIED`, which is tested. G1 is unchanged: Analyst **and**
Compliance Officer, on the approvals page.

## 9. Human override behaviour (`FR-CLS-003`)

- **A new revision, never an edit.** An override is a new classification revision: `requirement_classification`
  rows with `source = human`, no signal, the actor and the reason. Earlier revisions are kept. The requirement
  version is **not** touched, and its content hash is unchanged.
- **Who may override:**
  - a human Analyst of the project, and nobody else;
  - not a compliance officer, not an auditor;
  - not the pipeline actor (`classification.override` is human-only);
  - no one from another project.
- **What is refused:** an empty override, an override that changes nothing, an override without a reason, and an
  override of a version at `VALIDATED` or later. Relabelling would silently change what an approval covers, so that
  needs a new version.
- **What an override does:**
  - resolves the version's open label items as `overridden`;
  - is audited as O.2's `HUMAN_OVERRIDE`, with the before and after labels.

  E #5 calls this event `CLASSIFICATION_OVERRIDDEN`. O.2 is the closed taxonomy, and the E7 metric counts
  `HUMAN_OVERRIDE`.
- **Few-shot learning from overrides** (`FR-CLS-004`) is not implemented. Overrides are data for audit and for E7
  only.

## 10. Batch-mode workflow

```
analyst: POST /projects/{id}/sources (text or .txt/.md/.pdf/.docx, type, declared sensitivity)
analyst: POST /projects/{id}/analysis-runs {source_ids, domain: "LOAN"}
   GraphRunner → graph_run (RUNNING, started_by = analyst) + RUN_STARTED
   pipeline actor = system actor, identity = run id, role = Analyst in this project only
   analysis_graph (P3 subset, C.3):
     load_scope ──► extract_requirements ──► validate_extraction ──► persist_candidates ──► classify ──► END
         │  (versions only) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────► classify
         └─ any error ──► error_handler ──► END
   run → COMPLETED | FAILED + RUN_COMPLETED/RUN_FAILED (tokens, calls, cost)
human: review queue → accept / reject / override / merge / acknowledge
human: the P1 path — ANALYZED → VALIDATED → submit → G1 (Analyst + Compliance Officer)
```

**The nodes.**

- `extract_requirements` sends segments in windows of at most 40, one agent run per window. It records every
  schema-valid proposal as an `extraction_candidate` before anything is judged.
- `validate_extraction` is pure.
- `persist_candidates` allocates identifiers, creates the versions through P1, stores the criteria, moves each
  version `CANDIDATE → EXTRACTED` and raises review items.
- `classify` is one call per requirement. Where at least one label is valid, it records the revision and moves the
  version `EXTRACTED → CLASSIFIED`.
- A classification-only run takes `EXTRACTED` versions: after a failure, or after a merge.

**Routers** (`graph/routers.py`) read only the error list and the scope. Each returns a closed `Literal`.

**State** (`AnalysisState`) holds only ids and counts.

- The validation decision passes to persistence in the run's **transient** context. It is never in graph state.
- A test inspects every checkpoint of a real run: no statement, quote, speaker or transcript text is in any of
  them (D.1, D.3).

**Failure.**

- A node that fails records an agent run, a `NODE_FAILED` event and, where useful, a review item.
- It adds to `errors`, and the router sends the run to `error_handler`.
- Nothing advances past a failed node (C.8).
- A failed extraction produces **no** requirements, not partial ones.

## 11. P1 and P2 integration

**P1 is the only system of record**, and its mechanisms are used, not bypassed:

- **Identifiers.** `RequirementService.create_requirement` is called with ids allocated in batch order under a
  PostgreSQL advisory lock. The `(project_id, human_id)` unique constraint is the last defence.
- **Transitions.** `RequirementService.transition` performs them, with P1's guards: ≥ 1 source reference for
  `EXTRACTED`, ≥ 1 label for `CLASSIFIED`.
- **Withdrawal and new versions** use `RequirementService.withdraw` and `create_version`.
- **Versions stay immutable** with exact content hashes. G1, the baseline invariant and the lifecycle's 14 states
  are untouched. There is no `CONFLICTED` state.

**Three additive changes in P1's service**, all tested:

1. `RequirementContent.review_signal`. It is set once at creation and stays outside the content hash, as P1
   designed.
2. `build_context` counts current classification labels toward the `CLASSIFIED` guard. A manually set `category`
   still counts as before.
3. **A non-human actor may transition a version only to `EXTRACTED`, `CLASSIFIED` or `INVALID`.** Everything from
   analysis to approval is a human's to trigger. This is defence in depth beside policy rule 6.

**P2 is not changed.**

- P3 reuses P2's chunking helpers, the J.3 window sizes and the text extraction parsers.
- It adds a transcript-document segmenter to M5.
- Generic extraction and classification do not retrieve. E.1 gives neither role retrieval.
- P2 remains **P2 IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE — ET-06 PENDING**.

**Audit.** Everything goes through the one append-only, hash-chained `AuditService`, with references only.

| Group | Events |
|---|---|
| Run and node | `RUN_*`, `NODE_*` |
| O.2 content events | `SOURCE_INGESTED`, `EXTRACTION_PROPOSED`, `EXTRACTION_VALIDATED`, `CLASSIFICATION_PROPOSED`, `HUMAN_OVERRIDE` |
| Security | `PERMISSION_DENIED` on an egress refusal |
| New in P3 (P1/P2 precedent) | `REVIEW_ITEM_RAISED`, `REVIEW_ITEM_RESOLVED`, `REQUIREMENTS_MERGED` |

The pipeline's own actions are attributed to `system` with the run id. The run record names the human who started
it. Tests assert that no payload contains a statement, quote or transcript text.

## 12. Security and privacy boundaries

| Boundary | Enforced by | Proved by |
|---|---|---|
| One model boundary | `LLMGateway`; import-linter "LLM gateway depends on no application layer"; AST scan | security tests |
| Roles propose, never write | import-linter "Agent roles propose only"; roles take a gateway and return a proposal | AST and contract tests |
| Authority fields absent | `extra="forbid"` contracts; no id/state/approval/risk/regulation field | forged-output run produces nothing |
| No state change from model output | Transitions only by deterministic code; non-human actors capped at `CLASSIFIED` | pipeline and policy tests |
| Human decisions stay human | Policy rule 6: submit, withdraw, baseline, override, resolve, merge, add source, start run | policy matrix incl. superuser agent |
| Trust classes (Q.1) | Instructions only from locked templates + validated params; content fenced with nonce | injected-text test on the real request |
| No secret leaves | Gateway refuses any prompt containing a configured secret | secret-in-transcript test; nothing in audit or run records |
| No unmasked real data leaves | Gateway refuses unmasked, non-synthetic project content to a provider that leaves the machine; unknown providers assumed external | egress tests (refused; synthetic allowed) |
| Project isolation | Policy + scoped repositories; scope validated per run | cross-project run, queue, override, API 404 |
| Checkpoints carry no content | Ids and counts in state; decision in transient context | checkpoint inspection test |
| Immutability | ORM guard + PostgreSQL triggers (append-only; decide-once; resolve-once) | SQLite ORM tests + raw-SQL trigger tests |
| The key never leaks through the provider (§19) | The OpenAI adapter writes its own error text from status, type, code and request id only, and raises it outside the SDK exception's context. The provider's `repr` hides the client | adapter tests with a key-bearing 401 |
| The default suite cannot reach a provider (§19) | `tests/hermetic.py` sets `LLM_*` aside and stops `.env` being read | full suite run with the real `.env` present |

**Masking: the honest boundary.** `FR-ING-003` requires sensitive data to be classified and masked before any LLM
submission. **Masking is not implemented.** The approved roadmap builds it in P11. What P3 provides:

- **The stage in place.** The masking stage sits where J.2 puts it, and `NoMasking` records `not_masked` on every
  source.
- **A fail-closed egress rule.** Until masking exists, project content can leave the machine only if its uploader
  declared it **synthetic**. Real or unclassified data cannot reach an external model.
- **A declared, not detected, sensitivity** (`FR-ING-004`).

Since P3 closure an external provider exists: OpenAI, used only when configured (§19). The rule above applies to it
unchanged. Everything sent to it so far was synthetic (§19). Injection *detection* (Q.4) and capability tokens (P.1,
D10) are P11. The structural controls above are the defence in the meantime.

## 14. E1 evaluation

**Status (2026-09-22): computed. E1 = 0.967 on the synthetic reference benchmark E1-SYNTHETIC-v1. See §20.**
The rest of this section describes the harness and the state before the benchmark existed. It is kept as the
record.

*Before 2026-09-22:* no precision, recall or F1 figure existed for P3, and none was reported.

| Required input | State |
|---|---|
| Gold transcript #1: frozen, team-annotated, ≈ 60 gold requirements, manifest role `gold_transcript_1` | **Absent.** `data/gold/` is empty. The format is specified in `data/gold/README.md` |
| An extraction run by a **real model** | **Available since P3 closure.** The OpenAI provider exists (§19). A real-model run has been made, but only on the synthetic *development* transcript, which is not gold and cannot count as E1 |
| Human adjudication of every candidate pair | **Not possible.** Pairs are proposed against a gold set, and none exists |

**Gold item count:** none exists. **Predicted item count against gold:** none, because there is no gold set to run
against. The development-transcript run's 5 predictions (§19.5) are not E1 predictions.

**The harness is implemented and tested** (`services/evaluation/extraction_eval.py`, `scripts/evaluate_extraction.py`).
It works in five steps:

1. **Frozen gold set.** It loads the gold set only through its manifest. Every file's sha256 is checked, unlisted
   or missing files are refused, and spans are checked against the transcript (R.3, D16).
2. **Candidate pairs.** Code proposes pairs by span overlap on the same transcript, or by token-set Jaccard ≥ 0.5.
   This only widens what adjudicators see. **Adjudicators decide** each pair as `match` or `no_match`, and may add
   pairs. Disagreeing verdicts must be reconciled first.
3. **One-to-one matching.** A maximum bipartite matching (Kuhn's algorithm, deterministic) is taken over the pairs
   adjudicated `match`.
4. **The measures.** P = matched / predicted, R = matched / gold, F1 = 2PR / (P + R).
5. **Whether it counts.** The result counts as **E1 only if** the set is gold transcript #1, adjudication is
   complete, and a real model made every extraction call. Otherwise the report is titled **NOT E1** and says why.
   Precision, recall and F1 are withheld entirely for stub or scripted output.

The report also states the matching rule, gold and predicted counts, the gold manifest hash, providers, models and
prompt versions. It adds the ET-07 provisional target (F1 ≥ 0.75) as information only: *"to be re-baselined from
this measurement; not a pass mark"*. It lists the O.3 limitations.

Tests pin the arithmetic on hand-computed fixtures, including a case where one gold item has two candidate matches
but counts once. They show that tampering is refused and that a scripted run is never reported as E1. The test
`test_gold_transcript_one_for_the_p3_roadmap_exit` **skips**, visibly, until gold transcript #1 is added.

**The provisional target stays provisional.** ET-07 (0.75) is re-baselined *by* the first E1 measurement. So are
the targets for E2–E9 (analysis §P). P3 does not turn either into a guarantee.

## 15. Known limitations

- **No real model has been run.** Every AI behaviour is verified against scripted responses. That proves the
  mechanisms, not extraction quality, which is unmeasured until E1.
- **Masking is not implemented** (P11). Egress is restricted to synthetic data instead (§12).
- **Review signals are the model's self-report.** The thresholds are provisional and uncalibrated.
- **Quote matching is strict.** A model that paraphrases instead of quoting has the proposal rejected. That is
  safe, but a real model may show a high rejection rate until prompts are tuned (a new prompt version).
- **Near-duplicate detection is lexical** (token Jaccard). Project text is not embedded until masking exists (J.2).
- **Runs are synchronous**, in the request's transaction. A crash mid-run rolls the whole run back. Node-level
  resume with the PostgreSQL checkpointer is architecture C.7's, and not wired in P3.
- **Classification costs one call per requirement.** Batching labels is a later optimisation.
- **Candidates of a failed run stay `proposed`.** They are never judged, by design, and the run's `FAILED` status
  explains them.
- **The review queue is a foundation.** It has no assignment, ageing, blocking order or risk ordering (M.5). The
  only regenerate is re-classifying `EXTRACTED` versions.
- **Source documents** are limited to 200,000 characters in batch mode. Sensitivity is declared, not detected.
- **The egress secret guard** matches configured values exactly, of 8 characters or more.
- **The real model has been exercised only lightly.** One live pipeline run and two one-sentence calls, all on
  synthetic text written by the implementer (§19.5). Extraction quality remains unmeasured until E1.
- **Output shape is enforced by validation, not by the API.** OpenAI's JSON mode is not used (§19.1). Malformed
  output gets the gateway's one repair, then fails visibly. None occurred in the live checks.
- **An incomplete provider response is not used, and its tokens are not counted.** This covers a `status` other
  than `completed`, for example when an output limit is reached. It is recorded as `provider_unavailable`.
- **Cost is unknown.** No `LLM_PRICE_*` is configured for the model, so cost estimates are `None`, never guessed.
- **Deleting a project that has audit events** still fails on PostgreSQL. This is the pre-existing P11 item recorded
  in P2 §19. The P3 triggers themselves allow the cascade.

## 19. P3 closure: the OpenAI provider and real-model verification

At P3 closure the team selected a provider. This section records what that changed, what was verified with real
calls, and what it does **not** change: E1 is still pending (§14, §18).

### 19.1 Decision and configuration

- **Provider: OpenAI**, through the Responses API, behind the unchanged `LLMGateway`. It is recorded as a team
  decision in the architecture's decision-status entries only: ADR-006 status, the Q4 row, and section Y. The
  Anthropic proposal there is kept as history. `docs/01-analysis.md` is unchanged; its Q4 is answered for the
  provider, but no budget has been stated.
- **Model: configuration only.** `LLM_MODEL_DEFAULT`; the team's `.env` uses `gpt-5.6-luna`. No model name appears
  in the source, which a test checks. The reasoning tier (`LLM_MODEL_REASONING`) is still undecided and is not used
  in P3.
- **Settings**, read from the untracked `.env` or the environment:

  | Variable | Meaning |
  |---|---|
  | `LLM_PROVIDER=openai` | Selects the provider. `stub` stays the default |
  | `LLM_API_KEY` | The key. It lives in `.env` only (git-ignored: `.env`, `.env.*`, `!.env.example`) |
  | `LLM_MODEL_DEFAULT` | Required with `openai`. Settings refuse to load without it |
  | `LLM_BASE_URL` | Optional. Empty means the SDK's default endpoint |
  | `LLM_TEMPERATURE` | Optional. Empty means not sent |
  | `LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (60) | Per-request timeout |
  | `LLM_MAX_RETRIES` (3) | The only retry policy |
  | `LLM_FIXTURE_MODE` | `replay` answers from recordings and calls the provider on a miss; `live` always calls |
  | `LLM_PRICE_*` | Token prices. Unset, so cost is unknown |

- **The SDK** is `openai` 3.16.2. It is an optional extra (`pip install -e ".[openai]"`), also listed in `[dev]` so
  the adapter's offline tests run in CI. It is imported **lazily**, by `llm/openai_provider.py` only. The app and the
  default gateway never load it, which a subprocess test checks. Without the SDK, `LLM_PROVIDER=openai` fails at
  startup with the install hint.

**The first live calls found two things, and both were fixed within the rules:**

1. **The configured model rejects `temperature`.** OpenAI refused the first call: HTTP 400, `param=temperature`.
   ReqPilot had always sent its P0 default of 0.0. `LLM_TEMPERATURE` is now optional: unset by default, and sent only
   when configured. Nothing else about sampling is set.
2. **JSON mode is not used.** The API accepts its `json_object` output mode only if the word "json" appears in the
   *input*. In ReqPilot the input carries only fenced, untrusted data. Adding words there would put unversioned
   instructions in the data region, outside the prompt registry's hash. Instead, the JSON output contract stays
   where it was, in the versioned instructions. The gateway's strict parse, Pydantic schema, one repair and
   deterministic validation are unchanged. The contract is not weakened: anything other than one schema-valid JSON
   object fails.

**The default suite no longer reads `.env`.** The team's `.env` (`LLM_PROVIDER=openai` plus a key) broke two default
tests at once. Once `openai` became a valid value, it would have silently put the real key, and a real provider,
into any test that loads settings. `tests/hermetic.py`, imported first by `conftest.py`, prevents this:

- it sets every `LLM_*` shell variable aside;
- it sets `REQPILOT_DOTENV=off`, which `Settings` honours by not reading `.env`.

Only the opt-in live tests put the developer's configuration back, per test. The full suite was run with the real
`.env` present (§17).

### 19.2 The adapter

`src/reqpilot/llm/openai_provider.py`: `OpenAIProvider`, chosen by `build_provider` when `LLM_PROVIDER=openai`. It
implements the same one-method `complete` contract as every provider. Agents, services, the graph and the UI are
unchanged, and still reach a model only through the gateway.

| ReqPilot `LLMRequest` | OpenAI Responses API |
|---|---|
| `instructions` (template + output contract + data notice, assembled by the gateway) | `instructions` |
| each fenced `untrusted_content` block, unchanged | one `input_text` part of a single `user` message |
| `model_id` (from `LLM_MODEL_DEFAULT`) | `model` |
| `temperature`, `max_tokens`, when set | `temperature`, `max_output_tokens` |
| — | `store=False`: the provider is asked not to keep the response |

Nothing else is sent. The adapter adds no text of its own.

| OpenAI response | ReqPilot `LLMResponse` → `ModelMeta` → run record |
|---|---|
| `output_text` | `text`, which is still untrusted and goes to the gateway's parse and validation |
| `model` (as served) | `model_id` → `model_version` |
| `usage.input_tokens` / `output_tokens` | `tokens_in` / `tokens_out` → `agent_run` |
| wall-clock time | `latency_ms` |
| `id` | `response_id` → `ModelMeta.response_ids` → `agent_run.output_refs.provider_response_ids` |
| `status` ≠ `completed` | `provider_unavailable`. The partial output is not used |

**Failures** become the existing typed representation: `provider_unavailable` or `malformed_output`, never a crash.
The SDK's own retries are off (`max_retries=0`), so the gateway's bounded policy is the only one: up to 3 retries,
backing off 0.5, 1 and 2 s. Then there is at most one repair.

| SDK failure | ReqPilot | Retried? |
|---|---|---|
| timeout, connection error | `TransientProviderError` | yes, bounded |
| 408, 409, 429 rate limit, 5xx | `TransientProviderError` | yes, bounded |
| 429 `insufficient_quota` | `ProviderUnavailableError` ("quota exhausted") | no |
| 401 | `ProviderUnavailableError` ("check LLM_API_KEY") | no |
| 403 | `ProviderUnavailableError` ("the key may not have access to the configured model") | no |
| 404 | `ProviderUnavailableError` ("check LLM_MODEL_DEFAULT and LLM_BASE_URL") | no |
| other 4xx | `ProviderUnavailableError`, with HTTP status, `type`, `code`, `param`, `request_id` | no |
| anything else | `ProviderUnavailableError`, naming the exception class only | no |

**A provider's error message is never copied.** OpenAI's 401 text can include part of the key. Messages are written
from identifiers, each allowed only if it looks like an identifier. They are raised outside the SDK exception's
`except` block, so the original is neither the cause nor the context. The gateway records these adapter-written
messages; before, it recorded only the exception class.

### 19.3 Security and governance: unchanged, and re-verified

- **Egress.** The provider declares `leaves_machine = True`, so the gateway's rule applies in full. Unmasked content
  that is not declared synthetic is refused **before any call**; a test uses a fake client that records zero calls.
  Nothing real has been sent. Masking is still P11.
- **Secrets.** A prompt containing the configured key is refused before any call. The key appears in no error,
  `repr`, run record, audit event, log line, test or document. `.env.example` holds only empty placeholders, as the
  existing check requires.
- **Trust boundary.** Instructions and data travel in separate API positions. An injected "ignore all previous
  instructions" sentence reaches OpenAI only inside the fenced `user` message; a regression test asserts this. The
  synthetic workshop transcript itself contains an injected line: in the live run it produced no requirement, and
  nothing was approved.
- **Governance.** Model output still passes the same validation, span location, P1 transitions (nothing past
  `CLASSIFIED`) and review queue. The live run re-checked every one of these (§19.5). There is no new agent role,
  lifecycle state, gate or policy rule. P1 and P2 are unchanged.

### 19.4 Tests added at closure

- **`tests/unit/test_openai_provider.py`, 33 tests, offline.** They use a fake client and the SDK's real exception
  types, and cover:
  - configuration and initialisation: selection, replay wrapping, the client built with no SDK retries, the
    timeout and endpoint;
  - a missing key or model, a missing SDK, and no model name in the source;
  - the provider's `repr`;
  - a valid response with full provenance;
  - the request mapping and the injection boundary;
  - no adapter text; temperature and output limit sent only when set;
  - one repair, then `malformed_output`; a repaired response; incomplete responses; refusals;
  - 401 with a key-bearing message; no exception chaining;
  - timeouts, bounded; network recovery; rate limit; quota; 5xx; 400/403/404/422; unexpected exceptions;
  - unsafe identifiers;
  - the key-in-prompt and unmasked-egress refusals, both before any call;
  - the lazy import.
- **Security:** `test_only_the_openai_adapter_imports_the_openai_sdk`. The provider-construction scan now includes
  `OpenAIProvider(`. The P0 "no SDK installed" test became "the default configuration imports no provider SDK",
  checked in a fresh interpreter.
- **Opt-in, live, billable:** `tests/llm/test_openai_live.py`, 2 tests, marked `llm` and excluded by default. They
  also skip unless the developer's configuration selects `openai` with a key. Run them with
  `pytest -m llm tests/llm/test_openai_live.py -s`.
- **Updated:** the gateway's provider test now expects the selected provider's name, not Q4.

### 19.5 Real-model verification (not E1)

Run on 2026-09-21 on this machine, with the team's `.env` (`LLM_PROVIDER=openai`, `LLM_MODEL_DEFAULT=gpt-5.6-luna`).
**Only synthetic, fictional text was sent**:

- one invented requirement sentence;
- the synthetic development transcript `data/dev/transcripts/loan_intake_workshop_synthetic.md`, declared
  `SYNTHETIC`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| One-sentence classification (live test) | Completed first time. `gpt-5.6-luna`, 668 in / 129 out tokens, 3.7 s. Schema-valid, no repair. Labels `functional` 0.98 and `audit_reporting` 0.99, both accepted by deterministic validation |
| Full P3 pipeline on the synthetic workshop (live test) | `COMPLETED`: 6 calls (1 extraction, 5 classifications), 5,646 in / 2,575 out tokens, about 28 s. **5 requirements accepted**, 0 merged, 0 rejected, 1 review item, 5 classified |
| Invariants re-checked on the live run | Every source reference resolves to the exact source slice (`FR-EXT-007`). Every statement is declarative. Nothing past `CLASSIFIED`. No approval task. Every LLM agent run is stamped `openai` / `is_model` with its provider response ids. The audit chain verifies |
| Structured-output validity | 8 of 8 completed responses were schema-valid on the first attempt, with 0 repairs |

The 5 requirements the live run extracted, as stored:

1. "The system shall allow applicants to upload their income documents when they apply online."
2. "The system shall show applicants the status of their application at each stage."
3. "The system shall record every change to an application with who made it and when."
4. "The system shall respond within two seconds for most pages, even at month end."
5. "The system shall allow customers to export their statements."

**All requests made:** 11.

- **3 refused before generation** (HTTP 400): the `temperature` finding, and the JSON-mode finding plus one
  diagnostic call (§19.1).
- **8 completed:** 6,982 input and 2,932 output tokens in total.
- **Cost:** not computed. No price is configured, and none is assumed.

**What this is not.** It is not E1 and not a quality measurement. There was one run, on a transcript written by the
implementer rather than annotated independently, with no gold set to compare against. It shows that real model
output passes the unchanged P3 contract and governance, and nothing more.

## 20. E1 on the synthetic reference benchmark (P3 exit)

> Because ReqPilot is developed as a solo academic prototype, the E1 reference benchmark was synthetically
> generated and manually reviewed by the project author. It is intended as a development/evaluation benchmark and
> is not an independently annotated gold standard.

### 20.1 The benchmark: E1-SYNTHETIC-v1

- **Location:** `data/gold/e1_synthetic_v1/`, frozen on 2026-09-21. Manifest sha256 `6bce917368818c29…`. Its
  `BENCHMARK.md` has the full methodology, annotation guideline and coverage.
- **Transcript:** one fictional requirements interview for the retail loan origination portal. It has 70 speaker
  turns (71 segments) and 1,653 words. It contains no real people, data, credentials or regulations.
- **Designed cases:**
  - explicit and implicit requirements;
  - ambiguous and incomplete statements;
  - a requirement stated twice, and near-duplicates;
  - three conflicting pairs;
  - security-sensitive, regulatory, performance, availability and audit statements.
- **Designed distractors:** facilitator questions and a playback, an out-of-scope credit-policy remark, project-plan
  facts, and a prompt-injection line.
- **Reference: 60 requirements** (25 FR, 35 NFR). They are in the existing harness format, plus descriptive fields
  the harness ignores (`categories`, `phenomena`, `quote`). All 13 taxonomy categories are covered.
- **How the reference was made:**
  - The AI coding assistant (Claude, Anthropic) wrote the transcript and the reference.
  - It did so independently of ReqPilot and of the evaluated model, and **before** any ReqPilot run on this
    transcript.
  - Offsets were computed from exact quotes, not typed.
  - The project author reviewed the reference and accepted it as drafted. It was then frozen.
  - It is not revised because of results. Any correction is `E1-SYNTHETIC-v2`.
- **No leakage.** The runner gives ReqPilot only the transcript text. A test runs it with a scripted provider and
  asserts that no reference statement, id or field appears in any request.

### 20.2 The evaluated run

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Provider / model | OpenAI (Responses API) / `gpt-5.6-luna`, from `.env` |
| Prompts | `requirement_extraction@1.0.0` (sha256 `6ed48601…`), `requirement_classification@1.0.0` (sha256 `5fa3028a…`) |
| Run | `111b163e-616c-4767-82b1-49c8495127a1`, 2026-09-21 18:03 UTC |
| Configuration | Fixture mode `live`; temperature not sent; timeout 180 s; retries 3. No seed exists or is used |
| Pipeline | The unchanged P3 batch pipeline. The transcript is declared synthetic, and the egress guard is on |
| Outcome | Completed. 64 proposals: 60 accepted, 4 rejected by validation, 0 merged. 60 classified. 4 review items |
| API calls | **63**: 2 extraction windows, 1 repair, 60 classifications |
| Tokens | 51,033 in / 24,835 out |
| Cost | Not computed. No price is configured, and none is assumed |

Evidence files and commands for reproducing the run are in `docs/evaluation/e1-synthetic-v1/`.

### 20.3 Adjudication

- **Pairs.** The unchanged harness proposed **58** candidate pairs.
- **Suggestions.** The AI assistant suggested a verdict and a note for each pair, in `ADJUDICATION_SHEET.md`. All 58
  were `match`, with 4 flagged as borderline: R02, R25, R29, R38.
- **Verdicts.** The project author reviewed the sheet and **confirmed all 58 as `match`** on 2026-09-22. They are
  recorded in `adjudications.jsonl`. The verdicts are the author's, and they began as AI suggestions. That is stated
  here, not hidden.
- **Unpaired items,** which needed no verdict:
  - FR-LOAN-042, an extra prediction: the restated status need. R09 was already matched to FR-LOAN-006.
  - FR-LOAN-045, a false positive taken from the facilitator's playback ("a human underwriter").
  - R04, a miss: the implicit "show which documents are missing".
  - R24, a miss: the 500-user side of the 500 vs 2,000 conflict.

### 20.4 Results

**E1, from the unchanged harness (`e1_report.md`; the report counts it as E1):**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Reference items / predicted items | 60 / 60 |
| Matched (one-to-one) | 58 |
| **Precision** | **0.967** (58/60 = 0.9667) |
| **Recall** | **0.967** (58/60 = 0.9667) |
| **F1** | **0.967** |

**ET-07:** target F1 ≥ 0.75; actual 0.9667; **PASS against the provisional target**. The target is **re-baselined
and kept at 0.75**. One favourable, author-reviewed synthetic benchmark is not a sound basis for raising it (§20.5).
Thresholds and metric definitions were not changed.

**Supplementary descriptive figures** (`diagnostics.json`) are **not E1**, not approved metrics, and have no
targets:

| Aspect | Figure |
|---|---|
| Structured output | 62 LLM invocations, all succeeded. One extraction window needed the gateway's single repair, so 62 of 63 completed responses were schema-valid on the first attempt |
| Source spans | 60 of 60 stored spans reproduce their quote exactly from the stored transcript. 58 of 58 matched items' spans overlap the reference span |
| Distractors | The playback's 5 proposals: 4 were rejected by validation (quote under 3 words), 1 was accepted (FR-LOAN-045). The injected instruction produced no proposal. Nothing passed `CLASSIFIED`, and no approval task exists |
| Classification, on the 58 matched items | Label precision 0.44, recall 0.76, F1 0.56; exact label-set agreement 0.10. The model gives 2.48 labels per requirement, against 1 to 2 in the reference. This is a candidate finding for a classification prompt revision (a new prompt version, not part of P3) |
| Review signals | 4 review items (`unresolved_source`, the rejected playback proposals). Mean extraction signal: matched 0.975, unmatched 0.915. The signal separated the two groups only weakly |
| Audit | The evaluation project's hash chain verifies |

### 20.5 What this E1 does and does not show

**It demonstrates:**

- the P3 pipeline working end to end on a real model;
- extraction capability on a controlled synthetic benchmark;
- how classification behaves, including over-labelling;
- provenance handling: every span exact;
- reliable structured output;
- that ReqPilot can be evaluated repeatably: a frozen benchmark, a harness, recorded evidence.

**It does not demonstrate:**

- accuracy with real stakeholders;
- production performance in the financial sector;
- independently validated extraction accuracy;
- regulatory or legal correctness;
- generalisation to unseen organisations, domains or transcripts;
- production readiness.

**Why the score is likely optimistic:**

- **The benchmark is favourable by construction.** An LLM wrote the reference, and it knew ReqPilot's conventions
  (such as the "The system shall" form and the one-need-per-item rule). Stakeholder statements in the transcript are
  cleaner than real speech.
- **The same person built, reviewed and adjudicated.** The author built the system, reviewed the reference and
  confirmed the verdicts, and the verdicts started as AI suggestions.
- **It is one run on one transcript.** Model output varies from run to run.

### 20.6 Deviations, approved by the project author

1. **The "gold transcript #1" slot is filled by a synthetic reference benchmark.** Phase 0 O.1 and O.3 expect a
   human-annotated gold set. ReqPilot is a solo project with no annotation team, so the author approved an
   AI-generated, author-reviewed benchmark instead. The manifest's `"role": "gold_transcript_1"` is the harness's
   slot identifier. Its `role_note` says the set is not independent gold.
2. **"Sets targets for E2–E9" is met by following O.1.** Each E2–E9 target is set from that metric's own first
   measurement (E2 and E3 in P5, and so on), because P3 measures none of them.

### 20.7 Files added or changed for E1

- **Created:**
  - `data/gold/e1_synthetic_v1/`: the transcript, `requirements.jsonl`, `BENCHMARK.md`, `REVIEW_SHEET.md`,
    `manifest.json`
  - `scripts/run_e1.py`: glue around the existing harness and pipeline
  - `tests/integration/test_e1_benchmark.py`: 8 offline tests covering schema, loading, spans, taxonomy coverage,
    immutability, no real data, and no leakage
  - `docs/evaluation/e1-synthetic-v1/`: the evidence
- **Changed:**
  - `pyproject.toml`: `data/gold` excluded from ruff, so frozen files are never reformatted
  - `data/gold/README.md`
  - this document and `README.md`
- **Unchanged:**
  - the E1 harness, its metric definitions and ET-07;
  - the extraction and classification prompts, contracts, validation and rules;
  - the gateway and provider;
  - P1 and P2;
  - `docs/01-analysis.md` and `docs/02-architecture.md`.

## Decisions and deviations

No `[DESIGN]` decision is changed, no module or conceptual role is added, and the 13-role, 12-module, G1–G8 and
14-state baselines are unchanged. The places where P3 interprets or extends what the architecture spells out:

1. **The provider.** P3 was built with no network provider, as Y and Q4 required. At P3 closure the team selected
   OpenAI, and it was added as one provider class behind the unchanged gateway (§19).
2. **Masking is a seam with a fail-closed egress rule**, not an implementation (§12).
3. **Two tables beyond G's lists:**
   - `extraction_candidate`: every proposal, and what code decided about it;
   - `review_item`: the review-queue foundation.

   **Columns beyond the field lists:**
   - `requirement_classification.revision_no`, which makes overrides versioned;
   - `model_version.is_model`;
   - on `agent_run`: `attempts`, `error_code`, `review_signal`, `cost_estimate`, `finished_at`.

   `source_chunk.embedding` exists but stays empty.
4. **Policy rule 6** (§12) and eight new actions:
   - `source.create` / `source.read`;
   - `classification.propose` / `classification.override`;
   - `review.read` / `review.resolve`;
   - `requirement.merge`;
   - `run.record`.

   Also new: the **pipeline actor** (a system actor whose identity is the run id).
5. **Three additive changes to P1's service** (§11): `review_signal`, the label count, and the automated-transition
   cap.
6. **Audit events beyond O.2:** `REVIEW_ITEM_RAISED`, `REVIEW_ITEM_RESOLVED`, `REQUIREMENTS_MERGED`. The override
   uses O.2's `HUMAN_OVERRIDE`, not E #5's `CLASSIFICATION_OVERRIDDEN`.
7. **The model quotes; code computes offsets** (§7). The contract forbids unknown fields.
8. **Only exact duplicates are merged by code** (§5). Optional fields need their own supporting quote.
9. **D.2 places `candidates` in `AnalysisState`; P3 is stricter.** Proposals are persisted immediately, and the
   validation decision lives in transient context, so checkpoints hold no content.
10. **Runs are synchronous** and one-transaction (§15).
11. **Transcript documents are segmented by speaker turn**, because utterance records are P4's.
12. **§8 "category"** is the classification revision. P1's single `category` column remains the manually set
    category, and is left unset by extraction.
13. **Acceptance criteria are separate rows, bound to the version at creation.** They are not in the content hash,
    and a merge copies them to the successor.
14. **Migration `0005_p3_extraction`** is additive and reversible. A downgrade test proves P0–P2 are intact, and
    the revision-id length is now pinned.
15. **Phase-guard tests advanced one phase:** `test_migrations`, `test_p1_persistence`, `test_postgres_specific`,
    `test_api_health`.

## P4 readiness

P4 (Elicitation & clarification) can build on P3 without rework:

- **Model calls.** The gateway, prompt registry and trust classes are ready for role #2 (Stakeholder Interaction)
  and role #4 (Clarification). Each needs a template file and a contract.
- **Utterances.** An utterance can be fed to the same extraction role as one segment: `SegmentView` already carries
  a speaker and exact offsets. `chunk_transcript` (P2) exists for the utterance table.
- **Re-analysing a new version.** The review queue, classification revisions and `create_version` give P4's
  "answering a clarification creates a new version" a place to land. Re-classification of an `EXTRACTED` version is
  already a run mode.

What P4 must bring:

- the `utterance` table;
- `elicitation_graph`;
- its own interrupt/resume, with the PostgreSQL checkpointer;
- per-node commits, for resumable interviews (C.7).

The provider now exists (§19). P4's *"a scripted persona interview yields a usable requirement set"* can
therefore run on a real model, not only the mechanisms. P4's roles need their own versioned prompts, and the
interview text must be declared synthetic until masking exists.
